title: Design an Enterprise Knowledge Assistant (RAG over company documents)
prompt: Design a Q&A assistant over 5M internal documents (PDFs, slides, wikis) for 50,000 employees. Answers must cite sources and respect per-document access permissions.
clarifying: Document types, languages, and update frequency? How fresh must answers be?
Permission model: ACLs per document, groups, or row-level? How quickly must revocations apply?
Latency target (TTFT) and expected peak concurrency?
Quality bar: is a wrong answer worse than no answer? Need citations or human escalation?
Data residency / compliance constraints; can data go to a third-party LLM API?
estimation: 50k employees, 30% DAU, 8 queries/day → 120k queries/day ≈ 1.4 QPS avg, ~5 QPS peak
5M docs × ~20 chunks = 100M chunks; 768-d FP32 ≈ 307 GB raw (~460 GB with HNSW overhead) → shard or quantize (INT8 ≈ 4× less)
Per query ~4–6k input tokens, ~400 output → compare flash vs pro tiers for cost; quota is the real limit, not compute
architecture: Ingestion: connectors → object storage → parse/OCR → chunk → (optional LLM chunk context) → embed → index; event-driven via a queue, idempotent per doc version
Permissions: store ACL group ids as filterable metadata; resolve user → groups at query time; pre-filter in the vector DB
Query path: auth → query rewrite → hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense) → RRF → cross-encoder rerank → context assembly → LLM with citation prompt → guardrails → stream
Freshness: change events trigger incremental re-index; tombstones on delete/permission change
Quality loop: golden set, RAG-triad evals offline, sampled online evals, feedback capture
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Src[Doc sources] --> Q[Ingest queue]
  Q --> P[Parse + chunk]
  P --> E[Embed]
  E --> V[(Vector index + ACL metadata)]
  P --> B[(BM25 index)]
  U[User] --> API[API + AuthZ]
  API --> R[Hybrid retrieve + rerank]
  R --> V
  R --> B
  R --> L[LLM + guardrails]
  L --> U

deepDives.q: How do you guarantee a junior analyst never sees partner-only content?
deepDives.a: Pre-filter by ACL metadata inside the ANN query (not post-filter, which leaks via score/side-channels and hurts recall). Resolve group membership server-side from the identity provider, never trust client claims. Reindex or update metadata on permission change and keep a short cache TTL for group lookups. Add an audit log and a test suite of permission red-team queries. Also ensure caches (semantic cache, response cache) are keyed by access scope.

deepDives.q: Answers are wrong though retrieval 'looks fine'. How do you debug?
deepDives.a: Separate retrieval from generation. Measure context recall/precision against a labelled set; inspect chunking (tables, slide images), query rewriting, and top-k/rerank settings. If context contains the answer but the model ignores it, adjust prompt, ordering (lost-in-the-middle), or use a stronger model. Add faithfulness checks and abstain when evidence is weak.

deepDives.q: How do you handle 100M chunks?
deepDives.a: Quantize (scalar/PQ) to cut RAM, shard by tenant or hash with scatter-gather top-k, keep replicas for tail latency, use disk-based ANN for cold data, and route queries with metadata filters/partitions to reduce search space.

tradeoffs: Chunk size: small = precise but loses context; large = noisy and costly
Self-host open model vs managed API: data control vs ops burden and quality
Per-tenant indexes (isolation) vs shared index with filters (cost)
resumeTie: Deloitte Internal Asset Discovery (slide-to-image RAG on ChromaDB): explain what you shipped, then scale it with this design.
upgradeNotes: Rescope to 100M+ documents: ingestion throughput, index sizing, sharding
Add ACL-aware retrieval and permission-sync lag
Add freshness / delete propagation and re-embedding migration
Add eval plan: retrieval metrics + RAG triad + online signals

title: Design a Multi-Agent Customer Support System
prompt: Design an AI support system handling 100k tickets/day across chat and email: it should answer from the knowledge base, take actions (refund, reset, update order) safely, and escalate to humans.
clarifying: Which actions are allowed autonomously vs needing approval? Financial limits?
Channels, languages, SLAs (first response time, resolution time)?
Systems of record (CRM, billing, order management) and their APIs/latencies?
Success metrics: deflection rate, CSAT, escalation quality?
estimation: 100k tickets/day ≈ 1.2 QPS avg, ~10 QPS peak; chats multi-turn so concurrent sessions ≈ thousands
Per ticket 3–6 LLM calls + 2–4 tool calls; budget TTFT < 2 s using routing + parallel tool calls + streaming
architecture: Ingress normalizes channels into a ticket/session; guardrail layer (PII, injection, abuse) runs first with a small fast model
Router/supervisor classifies intent and dispatches to specialist agents (FAQ-RAG, order, billing, escalation)
State: session store (Redis) + durable checkpoints (Postgres) so any pod can resume
Tools behind a tool gateway: scoped credentials per agent, schemas, idempotency keys, per-action policy (amount limits, approvals)
Human handoff with summary and proposed action; feedback feeds eval datasets
Observability: trace per ticket; evals on sampled conversations
mermaid:
flowchart TD
  In[Chat / email] --> GR[Guardrails: PII + injection]
  GR --> SUP[Supervisor / router]
  SUP --> FAQ[FAQ RAG agent]
  SUP --> ORD[Order agent]
  SUP --> BIL[Billing agent]
  ORD --> TG[Tool gateway: scoped IAM + idempotency]
  BIL --> TG
  TG --> SOR[(CRM / billing / OMS)]
  SUP --> ST[(State: Redis + Postgres)]
  SUP --> HUM[Human escalation]

deepDives.q: A refund tool call fails after the order was already cancelled. What now?
deepDives.a: Treat the workflow as a saga: record each completed step in state, make each tool idempotent with a key, attempt the compensating action or route to human with full context when automatic compensation is unsafe. Never let the LLM decide to retry non-idempotent actions blindly; the orchestrator owns retry policy.

deepDives.q: How do you prevent prompt injection from a customer email causing a harmful action?
deepDives.a: Treat all user/retrieved text as untrusted. Enforce permissions in the tool gateway, not the prompt: scoped credentials, allow-lists, amount limits, confirmation for sensitive actions, and separation between reading untrusted content and holding powerful tools. Add injection classifiers and output validation.

deepDives.q: Agents loop or burn tokens. How do you stop that?
deepDives.a: Max steps and token budgets per ticket, loop detection (repeated tool/args), timeouts, and a deterministic fallback to human handoff.

tradeoffs: One strong model vs small router + specialists
resumeTie: Deloitte enterprise multi-agent support (24–48 h → near-instant): this is your flagship story.
upgradeNotes: Add agent-security threat model (indirect injection via customer email, tool misuse)
Add online eval: deflection, CSAT, escalation rate

title: Design a High-Throughput Model Serving Platform
prompt: Serve both a fine-tuned 7B LLM and a BERT-class NER model at 5,000 QPS combined, with P99 latency targets and cost efficiency on GPUs.
clarifying: Latency vs throughput per model; streaming for the LLM?
Traffic shape: steady or bursty? Multi-tenant?
Model update frequency and rollout safety?
estimation: 7B FP16 weights ≈ 14 GB; KV cache per token ≈ 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × 2 B — usually limits concurrency more than weights
NER model with dynamic batching on a GPU: often thousands of short requests/s per GPU → the LLM dominates GPU count
Autoscale on queue depth / tokens in flight, not CPU
architecture: Gateway → model router → per-model pools (vLLM/TGI for LLM; Triton/ONNX/TensorRT for NER)
Continuous batching + paged KV cache for LLM; dynamic batching with max-wait budget for NER
Quantization (INT8/FP8/AWQ) validated on a golden set
Autoscaler on queue depth with warm pools (model load takes minutes); separate pools for interactive vs batch
Rollouts: canary + shadow traffic, rollback by model version; metrics on TTFT, tokens/s, GPU utilization
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  C[Clients] --> GW[Gateway]
  GW --> R[Router]
  R --> L[LLM pool: vLLM]
  R --> N[NER pool: Triton + ONNX]
  L --> G1[(GPU nodes)]
  N --> G2[(GPU nodes)]
  A[Autoscaler: queue depth] --> L
  A --> N

deepDives.q: What is continuous batching and why does it matter?
deepDives.a: Instead of waiting for a whole batch to finish, the scheduler admits new sequences each decode iteration and retires finished ones, keeping GPUs busy and improving throughput and tail latency versus static batching.

deepDives.q: Cold starts when scaling GPU pods?
deepDives.a: Keep a minimum warm pool, preload weights from fast local/cached storage, use image/weight caching on nodes, scale ahead on predictive signals, and shed or queue with timeouts during ramp-up.

tradeoffs: Self-hosting vs API at your volume
resumeTie: Network18 NER serving; frame the cost savings honestly and be prepared to estimate GPU needs.
upgradeNotes: Add prefill/decode disaggregation and chunked prefill
Add multi-LoRA serving and speculative decoding trade-offs
Add GPU autoscaling on queue depth / KV utilisation

title: Design a ChatGPT-style Conversational Assistant
prompt: Design a multi-turn chat product with streaming responses for 10M weekly users, with conversation history, file uploads and model selection.
clarifying: Peak concurrent conversations and average turns per conversation?
Which models (self-hosted vs API)? Multi-model routing?
History retention, search over past chats, sharing?
Tools (web search, code), file types, and safety requirements?
estimation: 10M WAU, ~3M DAU × 10 messages/day = 30M msgs/day ≈ 350 QPS avg, ~1.5k QPS peak
Streaming: avg response 500 tokens at ~50 tok/s → ~10 s per response → concurrency ≈ 1.5k × 10 ≈ 15k open streams at peak
Context grows per turn; KV cache memory per concurrent sequence limits GPU concurrency if self-hosted
architecture: Edge: CDN/WAF → API gateway (auth, rate limit by user and tokens) → chat service over SSE/WebSocket
Chat service is stateless; conversation state in a durable store (Postgres/Cassandra) with recent turns cached in Redis
Context builder: system prompt + summarized older turns + recent turns + retrieved memory; enforce token budget
Inference router: pick model by plan/task, queue with priority, stream tokens back; fallback model on failure
Async: title generation, moderation, memory extraction, analytics through a queue
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  C[Client SSE] --> GW[Gateway: auth + limits]
  GW --> CS[Chat service]
  CS --> H[(History DB)]
  CS --> RC[(Redis cache)]
  CS --> CB[Context builder]
  CB --> RT[Model router]
  RT --> M1[Model pool A]
  RT --> M2[Model pool B]
  CS --> Q[Async queue]
  Q --> W[Moderation + memory + analytics]

deepDives.q: A user disconnects mid-stream. What happens?
deepDives.a: Keep generation decoupled from the connection: write tokens to a per-message buffer (Redis stream); the client resumes by message id and offset. Decide policy: cancel upstream generation on disconnect to save cost, or finish and persist. Persist the final message idempotently using a message id.

deepDives.q: How do you handle very long conversations?
deepDives.a: Rolling summaries plus recent window, retrieval over older turns/memory store, and hard token budgets per request. Summarize asynchronously after turns to avoid adding latency.

deepDives.q: How do you protect GPUs during a spike?
deepDives.a: Admission control with queue timeouts, priority tiers, load shedding with friendly errors, autoscaling on queue depth and tokens/s, and overflow to a secondary provider.

tradeoffs: SSE (simple, one-way, proxy friendly) vs WebSocket (bi-directional)
Dedicated capacity vs shared pool with priorities

title: Design an Enterprise LLM Gateway
prompt: Teams across a company call several LLM providers directly. Design a central gateway providing auth, quotas, routing, fallback, caching, guardrails and cost attribution.
clarifying: How many teams/apps and total QPS? Latency overhead allowed (e.g. < 20 ms)?
Providers and models; streaming required? Self-hosted models too?
Budget enforcement: hard stop or alert? Per team, per key, per user?
Compliance: prompt logging, PII redaction, regional data rules?
estimation: 2,000 req/s peak, mostly streaming, average 3 s → ~6k concurrent connections; gateway must be async and horizontally scalable
Token metering: log input/output tokens per request — 2,000 × 86,400 ≈ 170M events/day max → write via queue to analytics store
architecture: Stateless gateway pods (async) behind a load balancer; unified OpenAI-compatible API surface
AuthN (API keys/OIDC) → policy engine (allowed models, budgets) → rate limiter (Redis token bucket on RPM and TPM with reservation) → cache → router → provider adapter
Router: rules + cost/latency/health-aware; complexity classifier to send easy prompts to a cheaper model; circuit breakers and region/provider fallback
Guardrails hooks: PII redaction, injection checks, output filters (configurable per team)
Metering: emit usage events asynchronously → queue → warehouse; dashboards and budget alerts
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[Apps] --> G[Gateway]
  G --> AU[Auth + policy]
  AU --> RL[Rate limit RPM/TPM]
  RL --> CA[Cache]
  CA --> RO[Router + fallback]
  RO --> P1[Provider A]
  RO --> P2[Provider B]
  RO --> P3[Self-hosted]
  G --> U[Usage events]
  U --> W[(Warehouse + budgets)]

deepDives.q: How do you enforce a TPM quota when output length is unknown?
deepDives.a: Reserve tokens = input count + max_tokens (or an estimate) before the call, then reconcile with actual usage after completion and refund the difference. Use Redis atomic scripts keyed by team and model. For streaming, update on completion; also cap max_tokens.

deepDives.q: Gateway is a single point of failure — how do you make it safe?
deepDives.a: Stateless replicas across zones, minimal critical-path dependencies (local policy cache, Redis degradation mode that fails open/closed deliberately), async metering, canary deploys, and client SDK fallback to direct provider only for approved emergencies.

deepDives.q: How does routing by complexity avoid quality regressions?
deepDives.a: Shadow-evaluate router decisions against a golden set, start conservative (route only clearly simple intents), monitor quality metrics per route, and allow per-team overrides.

tradeoffs: Fail-open vs fail-closed on limiter outage
Semantic cache gains vs leakage risk
resumeTie: Cross-platform AI architecture with $1.3M+ savings — frame as cost governance and routing.
upgradeNotes: Add routing cascades and cost-per-resolved-task metric

title: Design an AI Document-Processing & Reporting Automation Platform
prompt: Design a platform that ingests thousands of semi-structured documents daily, extracts structured data with LLMs, validates it, and generates scheduled reports for business users.
clarifying: Document formats, volume per day, accuracy requirement per field?
Human-in-the-loop for low-confidence fields?
Report cadence and consumers; auditability requirements?
estimation: 50k docs/day × ~10 pages; LLM extraction ~3k tokens/page → ~1.5B tokens/day → choose cheaper tier + batch APIs + caching of repeated templates
Throughput bursts at month end — queue absorbs spikes
architecture: Ingest → object storage → parse/OCR → classify doc type → schema-driven extraction (LLM with structured output) → validation rules + confidence → exceptions queue for humans
Orchestrated pipeline (workflow engine) with per-doc idempotency, retries and lineage
Warehouse (BigQuery) for validated data; scheduled report generation (SQL + LLM narrative) with citations to source rows
Evals: field-level accuracy on labelled set, drift monitoring per doc type
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  D[Documents] --> S[(Object store)]
  S --> OCR[Parse / OCR]
  OCR --> CL[Classify]
  CL --> EX[LLM extraction]
  EX --> VA[Validation + confidence]
  VA -- low conf --> HR[Human review]
  VA --> WH[(Warehouse)]
  HR --> WH
  WH --> RP[Scheduled reports]

deepDives.q: How do you make extraction trustworthy?
deepDives.a: Constrain output with schemas, validate with deterministic rules (totals, formats, cross-field checks), calibrate confidence (self-consistency or logprobs where available), route low-confidence items to humans, and track field-level accuracy against a golden set.

deepDives.q: How do you cut cost 10×?
deepDives.a: Template/layout detection to skip LLM for known forms, smaller models for easy doc types, batch/async APIs, caching, and only invoking a stronger model on validation failure (cascade).

tradeoffs: Human review capacity vs accuracy target
resumeTie: Network18 reporting automation (3,500+ man-hours saved) and BigQuery/PySpark pipelines.
